newsitem.title: USA: Sallie Mae group claims near victory on reorganization.
newsitem.headline: Sallie Mae group claims near victory on reorganization.

text.p: A dissident group of Student Loan Marketing Association shareholders Friday claimed near victory for their proposal to reorganize the agency, even though the votes they have received so far fall short of a majority.
"We are extremely pleased by this strong vote in support of our proposals," said Albert Lord, a Sallie Mae director and leader of the dissident group, after a special shareholder meeting.

Sallie Mae, a government sponsored enterprise formed by Congress, buys guaranteed loans from lenders so that they have funds to make more loans. Under Lord's plan, the agency would be privatised and make student loans directly instead.

Lord's group, called the Committee to Restore Value, said it received nearly 23 million votes in favour and 15 million against the proposal. That leaves votes on about 13 million shares uncast while the tallying continues through May 29.
"While we are enjoying this 60/40 margin for the time being over the management slate, I think it is only appropriate to tell you this margin was a very, very difficult achievement," Lord said.

Meanwhile, Sallie Mae has scheduled a meeting for its own privatisation plan and slate of directors for May 15 and is challenging in court the validity of the group's special meeting Friday and its votes.

"It is clear that the (Committee to Restore Value) failed to get the support for their plan that they were seeking and we are looking forward to the May 15 meeting which is the one that really counts," a Sallie Mae spokeswoman said.

Nonetheless, Lord said he is confident his group will receive the majority votes it needs, as mandated by Congress last year when it enacted legislation requiring Sallie Mae, with nearly $50 billion in assets, to go private or be liquidated altogether.
After the shareholder vote, Lord urged Sallie Mae Chairman William Arceneaux to call a special board meeting to install the dissident group's slate of directors.
"I see incredible opportunities in the huge vibrant growing student loan marketplace," Lord said.
Sallie Mae's stock rose $4.375 to $121.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
